```markdown
# Strapi CMS

## Overview
Content Management System for defcon.run event content.

## Access
- **Admin Panel**: https://cms.defcon.run/admin
- **API Base**: https://cms.defcon.run/api

## Authentication
Login via auth.defcon.run OIDC. Users must have 'cms' in their services claim.

To request CMS access:
1. Contact an administrator
2. They will add 'cms' to your services claim in auth database

## Content Types

### Pages
- Endpoint: /api/pages
- Fields: title, slug, content, excerpt, published

### Announcements  
- Endpoint: /api/announcements
- Fields: title, content, priority, publishedAt, expiresAt, pinned

### Events
- Endpoint: /api/events
- Fields: title, description, location, startTime, endTime, category

## API Usage

### Public Content (no auth required)
\`\`\`bash
# List pages
curl https://cms.defcon.run/api/pages

# Filter by field
curl 'https://cms.defcon.run/api/pages?filters[slug]=home'

# Include relations
curl 'https://cms.defcon.run/api/pages?populate=*'
\`\`\`

### Protected Content (requires API token)
\`\`\`bash
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <api-token>' \
  https://cms.defcon.run/api/protected-content
\`\`\`

## Architecture
- Master (us-east-1): Read/write, serves /admin
- Workers (us-east-1, ca-central-1): Read-only, serve /api
- Sync delay: Up to 5 minutes for content propagation
```

title: Create CMS failover runbook
description:
Document failover and recovery procedures for CMS.

Create docs/runbooks/CMS-Failover.md:

```markdown
# CMS Failover Runbook

## Scenario 1: Master Instance Unhealthy

### Symptoms
- 502/503 errors on /admin/*
- CloudWatch alarm: CMS Master Unhealthy
- No new WAL segments in S3

### Impact
- Content editing unavailable
- Workers continue serving cached content (read-only)

### Resolution
1. Check ECS task status:
   \`\`\`bash
   aws ecs describe-services --cluster dc34-app --services cms-master --region us-east-1
   \`\`\`

2. Check task logs for errors:
   \`\`\`bash
   aws logs tail /ecs/dc34-cms-master --region us-east-1
   \`\`\`

3. Force new deployment:
   \`\`\`bash
   aws ecs update-service --cluster dc34-app --service cms-master --force-new-deployment --region us-east-1
   \`\`\`

## Scenario 2: Worker Instances Unhealthy

### Resolution
- Workers can be restarted independently
- New workers restore from S3 automatically

\`\`\`bash
aws ecs update-service --cluster dc34-app --service cms-worker --force-new-deployment --region <region>
\`\`\`

## Scenario 3: Database Corruption

### Resolution - Point-in-Time Recovery
1. Stop master service
2. Identify recovery point in S3:
   \`\`\`bash
   aws s3 ls s3://$BUCKET/db/generations/ --recursive
   \`\`\`

3. Restore to specific point:
   \`\`\`bash
   litestream restore -config litestream.yml -timestamp '2024-01-01T12:00:00Z' /data/strapi.db
   \`\`\`

4. Restart master service

## Scenario 4: Complete Recovery

If all instances lost:
1. Deploy fresh infrastructure (terragrunt apply)
2. Master will restore from S3 on startup
3. Workers will sync from restored master
```

title: Create Litestream sync script for workers
description:
Create litestream-sync.sh for worker DB synchronization.

**File:** apps/run.cms/app/litestream-sync.sh
```bash
#!/bin/sh
set -e

CONFIG="/etc/litestream/litestream.yml"
DB_PATH="/data/strapi.db"
SYNC_INTERVAL=300  # 5 minutes

echo "[litestream-sync] Starting worker sync process..."
echo "[litestream-sync] Config: $CONFIG"
echo "[litestream-sync] Database: $DB_PATH"
echo "[litestream-sync] Sync interval: ${SYNC_INTERVAL}s"

# Initial restore from S3 (only if DB doesn't exist)
if [ ! -f "$DB_PATH" ]; then
    echo "[litestream-sync] Database not found, restoring from S3..."
    litestream restore -config "$CONFIG" -o "$DB_PATH" "$DB_PATH"
    
    if [ ! -f "$DB_PATH" ]; then
        echo "[litestream-sync] ERROR: Failed to restore database from S3"
        echo "[litestream-sync] This may be a new deployment - master must push first"
        # Create empty DB so Strapi can start (it will be empty until next sync)
        touch "$DB_PATH"
    else
        echo "[litestream-sync] Database restored successfully"
    fi
else
    echo "[litestream-sync] Database exists, will sync from S3"
fi

# Periodic sync loop
while true; do
    sleep $SYNC_INTERVAL
    echo "[litestream-sync] Syncing database from S3..."
    
    # Only restore if replica has newer data
    if litestream restore -config "$CONFIG" -if-replica-newer -o "$DB_PATH" "$DB_PATH" 2>&1; then
        echo "[litestream-sync] Sync completed"
    else
        echo "[litestream-sync] Sync skipped (no newer data) or failed"
    fi
done
```

**Make executable:**
```bash
chmod +x apps/run.cms/app/litestream-sync.sh
```

**How it works:**
1. On startup: restores DB from S3 if not exists
2. Then loops forever, syncing every 5 minutes
3. Uses -if-replica-newer to only download if S3 has newer data
4. Logs all operations to stdout for CloudWatch

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] litestream-sync.sh created in apps/run.cms/app/
- [ ] Script is executable (chmod +x)
- [ ] SYNC_INTERVAL=300 (5 minutes)
- [ ] Uses -if-replica-newer for efficient syncs

title: Create CMS app Dockerfile with Strapi + Litestream
description:
Create app container with Strapi v5, Litestream, and supervisord.

**Reference:** https://github.com/whereiskurt/defcon.run.33/blob/main/apps/strapi/site-tld/Dockerfile.prod

**Prerequisites:**

**File: apps/run.cms/app/Dockerfile.app**
```dockerfile
# Creating multi-stage build for production
FROM node:20-alpine AS build
RUN apk update && apk add --no-cache build-base gcc autoconf automake zlib-dev libpng-dev vips-dev > /dev/null 2>&1
ARG NODE_ENV=production
ENV NODE_ENV=${NODE_ENV}

WORKDIR /opt/
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm config set fetch-retry-maxtimeout 900000 -g && npm install --only=production
ENV PATH=/opt/node_modules/.bin:$PATH
WORKDIR /opt/app
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

# Creating final production image
FROM node:20-alpine
RUN apk add --no-cache curl vips-dev supervisor sqlite

# Install Litestream
ARG LITESTREAM_VERSION=0.3.13
RUN wget -q https://github.com/benbjohnson/litestream/releases/download/v${LITESTREAM_VERSION}/litestream-v${LITESTREAM_VERSION}-linux-amd64.tar.gz -O /tmp/litestream.tar.gz \
    && tar -xzf /tmp/litestream.tar.gz -C /usr/local/bin \
    && rm /tmp/litestream.tar.gz \
    && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/litestream

ARG NODE_ENV=production
ENV NODE_ENV=${NODE_ENV}

# Create data directory for SQLite
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown node:node /data

# Create litestream config directory
RUN mkdir -p /etc/litestream

WORKDIR /opt/
COPY --from=build /opt/node_modules ./node_modules
WORKDIR /opt/app
COPY --from=build /opt/app ./
ENV PATH=/opt/node_modules/.bin:$PATH

# Copy runtime configs
COPY supervisord.master.conf /etc/supervisord.master.conf
COPY supervisord.worker.conf /etc/supervisord.worker.conf
COPY litestream.master.yml /etc/litestream/litestream.master.yml
COPY litestream.worker.yml /etc/litestream/litestream.worker.yml
COPY litestream-sync.sh /usr/local/bin/litestream-sync.sh
COPY entrypoint.sh /entrypoint.sh

RUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/litestream-sync.sh /entrypoint.sh

RUN chown -R node:node /opt/app
EXPOSE 1337

ENTRYPOINT ["/entrypoint.sh"]
```

**File: apps/run.cms/app/entrypoint.sh**
```bash
#!/bin/sh
set -e

echo "Starting CMS in ${STRAPI_MODE:-worker} mode..."

# Select supervisord config based on STRAPI_MODE env var
if [ "$STRAPI_MODE" = "master" ]; then
    echo "Configuring as MASTER (Litestream replicate)"
    cp /etc/supervisord.master.conf /etc/supervisord.conf
    cp /etc/litestream/litestream.master.yml /etc/litestream/litestream.yml
else
    echo "Configuring as WORKER (Litestream restore/sync)"
    cp /etc/supervisord.worker.conf /etc/supervisord.conf
    cp /etc/litestream/litestream.worker.yml /etc/litestream/litestream.yml
fi

exec /usr/bin/supervisord -c /etc/supervisord.conf
```

**Key differences from run.auth/run.human:**
- NOT a Next.js app - no static asset extraction
- Based on DC33 Dockerfile.prod pattern
- Includes vips-dev for image processing
- Includes Litestream binary (~10MB)
- Includes supervisord for process management
- STRAPI_MODE env var selects master/worker config
- Exposes 1337 (not 3000)
- Uses multi-stage build for smaller image

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Dockerfile builds successfully: `docker build -f Dockerfile.app -t test .`
- [ ] Image includes: node, supervisord, litestream, sqlite, vips
- [ ] Litestream binary works: `docker run test litestream version`
- [ ] Entrypoint selects correct config based on STRAPI_MODE
- [ ] Image size reasonable (<600MB)

title: Test media upload and CloudFront delivery
description:
Test media upload workflow with S3 and CloudFront OAC.

## How It Works

1. **Upload Path**: Strapi uploads to S3 with prefix `{region}/cms/`
   - Example S3 key: `use1/cms/bunnyhead.png`
   
2. **URL Construction**: Strapi constructs URLs as:
   - `baseUrl` + `/` + `rootPath` + `/` + `filename`
   - Example: `https://cms.defcon.run/use1/cms/bunnyhead.png`

3. **CloudFront Routing**: `/{region}/cms/*` routes to CMS media S3 origin via OAC

## Test Steps

1. **LOGIN**
   - Navigate to https://cms.defcon.run/use1/admin
   - Authenticate via OIDC

2. **UPLOAD MEDIA**
   - Click 'Media Library' in sidebar
   - Click 'Add new assets'
   - Upload a test image (e.g., test-image.png)
   - Wait for upload to complete

3. **VERIFY S3 STORAGE**
   ```bash
   # List uploaded files - should be at use1/cms/ prefix
   aws s3 ls s3://uploads-dc34-cms-media-use1-80a6b349/use1/cms/ --profile application
   ```

4. **GET PUBLIC URL**
   - In Strapi Media Library, click on the uploaded image
   - Copy the URL
   - Expected format: `https://cms.defcon.run/use1/cms/test-image.png`

5. **VERIFY CLOUDFRONT DELIVERY**
   ```bash
   curl -I 'https://cms.defcon.run/use1/cms/test-image.png'
   # Check headers:
   # - Content-Type: image/png
   # - X-Cache: Hit from cloudfront (after first request)
   ```

6. **CLEANUP**
   - Delete test image from Media Library
   - Verify S3 object is removed

## Infrastructure Components

- **S3 Bucket**: `uploads-dc34-cms-media-{region}-{suffix}`
- **CloudFront OAC**: `oac-cms-media-{region}-defcon.run`
- **Bucket Policy**: Managed by CloudFront module with `AWS:SourceArn` condition

title: Create Litestream master configuration
description:
Create litestream.master.yml for continuous replication.

**File:** apps/run.cms/app/litestream.master.yml
```yaml
# Litestream configuration for CMS master
# Continuously replicates SQLite WAL to S3

dbs:
  - path: /data/strapi.db
    replicas:
      - type: s3
        bucket: ${CMS_LITESTREAM_BUCKET}
        path: db
        region: ${AWS_REGION}
        sync-interval: 1s
        snapshot-interval: 1h
        retention: 168h  # 7 days
        retention-check-interval: 1h
```

**Environment variables (from ECS task definition):**
- CMS_LITESTREAM_BUCKET: S3 bucket name (from SSM)
- AWS_REGION: us-east-1
- AWS credentials: from ECS task role (no explicit keys needed)

**How it works:**
1. Monitors /data/strapi.db for changes
2. Pushes WAL segments to S3 every 1 second
3. Creates snapshots hourly
4. Retains 7 days of history for point-in-time recovery

**S3 structure created:**
```
s3://bucket/db/
├── generations/
│   └── <generation-id>/
│       ├── snapshots/
│       │   └── <timestamp>.lz4
│       └── wal/
│           └── <segment>.lz4
└── latest
```

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] litestream.master.yml created in apps/run.cms/app/
- [ ] Database path is /data/strapi.db
- [ ] sync-interval is 1s for near-realtime replication
- [ ] retention is 168h (7 days)

title: Prowler not counting muted findings correctly - shows wrong counts
description:
## Problem
The GitHub Actions summary shows 'Muted: 0' even though Prowler correctly identifies 13 muted findings.

## Evidence
- Prowler console output: 15 Failed, 0 Passed, 13 Muted
- GitHub summary: High: 15, Muted: 0

## Root Cause
The jq queries in prowler-scan.yml used wrong status_id values:
- Code assumed `status_id == 5` for muted/suppressed
- Actual OCSF format uses `status_id == 3` and `status == "Suppressed"`

## Fix
Changed jq queries to use the string `status` field instead of `status_id`:
- Non-muted: `select(.status != "Suppressed")`
- Muted: `select(.status == "Suppressed")`

## Location
.github/workflows/prowler-scan.yml:105-112
close_reason: Fixed jq queries to use status=Suppressed instead of status_id=5

title: Define CMS master service in service.hcl
description:
Define the cms-master ECS service in service.hcl.

Service configuration:
```hcl
# Master service - handles admin/write operations
cms_master_service = {
  name          = "cms-master"
  regions       = ["us-east-1"]  # SINGLE REGION ONLY
  cluster_name  = "app"
  task_family   = "cms-master"
  desired_count = 1  # Single instance, no scaling

  service_discovery = {
    name           = "cms-master"
    container_name = "cms-app"
  }

  load_balancers = [
    {
      type                  = "alb"
      container_name        = "cms-nginx"
      container_port        = 443
      target_group_protocol = "HTTPS"
      health_check_path     = "/_health"
      health_check_protocol = "HTTPS"

      health_check = {
        healthy_threshold   = 2
        unhealthy_threshold = 3
        timeout             = 10
        interval            = 30
        matcher             = "200-399"
      }

      listener = {
        port         = 443
        protocol     = "HTTPS"
        host_headers = ["cms.defcon.run"]
        # Priority routing: /admin/* goes to master
        path_patterns = ["/admin/*", "/admin"]
      }
    }
  ]

  autoscaling = {
    enabled = false  # CRITICAL: Single writer, never scale
  }
}
```

IMPORTANT:
- Master handles ALL /admin/* routes (content editing)
- Must NOT autoscale (single writer constraint)
- Higher health check timeout for Strapi cold starts
- Only runs in us-east-1
